featured_reviews.name: tushar kardam
featured_reviews.review_text:
This is a single-tower society, and I’ll break my review into three parts: Worth, Safety, and Challenges.

Worth: 1/5

If you’re planning to buy a flat here, don’t.

The builder has cut corners everywhere. Cheap materials, poor planning, and a layout designed to maximize sales rather than residents’ comfort. The building is split into A Wing, B Wing, A1, and B1, creating a bizarre class system where certain residents get privileges others don’t. A and B Wing residents have access to facilities and parking inside the compound, while A1 and B1 residents are treated like second-class citizens.

What’s worse is that maintenance is already failing despite the building being relatively new. I have water leakage from the floor above, and even after multiple complaints, nothing has been fixed.

For renters, it’s an even worse deal. Asking rents are touching ₹50,000 for a 1.5 BHK, which is absurd considering the quality of construction, maintenance, and overall living experience.

Safety: 1/5

Parking is a disaster, especially for A1 and B1 residents who are forced to park outside on public roads. My bike has been vandalized multiple times, costing me over ₹11,000 in repairs.

The biggest concern, however, is fire safety. The fire suppression pipeline appears to run only up to the main entrance rather than throughout the building. I’m not a fire safety expert, but if that’s actually the case, it’s alarming. In the event of a fire originating inside an apartment, I have serious doubts about how effective the system would be.

Challenges: 2/5

The building is right next to a public park, which means constant noise throughout the day. Mornings, afternoons, evenings—there’s always something happening. Your only solution is to keep the windows shut.

Installing an AC is unnecessarily expensive because the outdoor unit placement and duct planning are terrible. I had to spend more than ₹5,000 extra just on additional copper piping because the builder couldn’t design a sensible layout.

The lifts feel like the cheapest option available—slow, cramped, and without even basic ventilation. The gym exists mostly for marketing brochures; several essential pieces of equipment are missing.

Overall, this society looks far better in advertisements than it performs in reality. Between the poor construction quality, questionable planning decisions, maintenance issues, safety concerns, and inflated rents, I would strongly advise potential buyers and tenants to look elsewhere.

featured_reviews.name: Ishan K
featured_reviews.review_text:
Read this if you are planning to buy or rent here.

For rent prospects:
1.	There is visible discrimination toward tenants. Guards won’t allow tenants to park their vehicles inside the compound. Even if parking is allowed, people litter, spit, and do all kinds of nonsense from their windows.
2.	Most residents belong to the same social circle, so you won’t have any ground to argue, even on sensible issues.
3.	Our landlord forcefully imposed a 1-year lock-in within a 2-year agreement, and within 10 days of shifting, he started sending brokers to show the flat. If the owner wants to sell, there is no reason to put the property on rent.
4.	At any day or time, people barge into the flat with others to show it, often without any prior notice. As a so-called goodwill gesture, you’re expected to cooperate even when you’re sleeping or dealing with personal matters.
5.	There are water issues, constant noise from people gathering in the ground next to the building, and continuous flight noise due to the nearby flight path.
6.	Food delivery apps take a long time—usually 45–60 minutes—since most restaurants are on the west side or toward Pant Nagar.

For buyers:
1.	The builder has constructed the flats on a cookie-cutter budget. Don’t fall for the lobby view.
2.	Most materials, including plaster and tiles, are poor quality. You can literally make a hole with something as simple as a pencil.
3.	The flat planning is very poor. From the main door, the bedroom is clearly visible. The basic public–private separation followed in good house design is completely ignored.
4.	There is a serious mosquito problem in the area. I’ve tried everything from repellents to electric bats, but still have to close doors only after killing mosquitoes in each room.
5.	People will object to others cooking non-vegetarian food, yet they often cook it themselves.

The only pros of this locality are close proximity to the metro or station, plenty of barber shops depending on how much you need them, and a few general stores and a vegetable market.

It has really good security as well.
